findings.title: Copy-paste error in requireNonNull message
findings.body: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") reuses the previous line's check on grantType and labels the message as if it were for rawTokenId. The intended line is almost certainly Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"). With this typo, if a caller passes a null rawTokenId, the failure message says "Null rawTokenId not allowed" but does so from the grantType check, while the rawTokenId is never validated at all and is allowed to be null.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher does not actually verify the expected grant type
findings.body: In the new isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut) matcher: (a) the condition is inverted ('return false' when the substring equals the expected grant), and (b) the offset is wrong. The token id format produced by encodeTokenId is ST(2) + TT(2) + GT(2) + ':' + rawId, so the grant shortcut occupies characters at 0-indexed positions 4 and 5 (substring(4,6)). The matcher uses substring(3,5), which is the last char of the token type and the first char of the grant type ("ta" for the example in the PR description, "ac" would actually be at substring(4,6)). Because of the offset, the substring will never equal the expected grant, and because of the inversion the branch returns false instead of true even if it did. As a result, every call site that now uses isAccessTokenId(...) (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) effectively only checks that the token id has the form 'XXXXXX:UUID' and does not actually verify the grant type. The whole point of these test changes - to detect wrong grant shortcut mapping after this PR - is silently lost.

findings.title: New abstract method on the grant SPI breaks every external implementation
findings.body: Adding String getShortcut() as an abstract method on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is a binary- and source-incompatible change for every third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation (including in the many extensions Keycloak ships). Any out-of-tree impl compiled against the previous version will fail to load at runtime with AbstractMethodError and any extension maintainer will fail to compile against the new version. The field is internal SPI (server-spi-private), but it is still on an interface implemented by SPIs in extension points (Ciba, Device, TokenExchange, UMA Permission, etc.). At a minimum the new method needs a default implementation (e.g. default returning getId()) and the existing built-in factories should override it.

findings.title: Removed public Context copy constructor
findings.body: The diff removes the public Context(Context context) copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType.Context (the rest of the constructors remain). Even for 'internal' SPI in the server-spi-private module, this is a binary-incompatible removal: existing compiled callsites and any extension using that constructor will fail with NoSuchMethodError at runtime. If a copy constructor was no longer needed, that should be confirmed; if it was, it should be retained.

findings.title: getShouldUseLightweightToken promoted from package-private instance to public static
findings.body: The method signature was changed from 'boolean getShouldUseLightweightToken(KeycloakSession session)' (package-private instance) to 'public static boolean getShouldUseLightweightToken(KeycloakSession session)'. Subclasses outside this package that overrode the package-private instance version will now have two distinct methods (the inherited one and their override) and call sites using their subclass reference would still hit the parent's version. It would be safer to keep an instance-method shim (e.g. protected boolean getShouldUseLightweightToken(...) that delegates to a public static) so that subclasses continue to work, or document and version the change explicitly.

findings.title: Duplicated-grant-shortcut validation fires after entries already overwritten, error message misleading
findings.body: In postInit the loop does grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName) for each grant. If two factories return the same shortcut, the later entry silently overwrites the earlier one in grantsByShortcuts, but grantsToShortcuts still contains both grant ids. The only validation is the post-loop size check, which catches it but the exception message just says 'Make sure there is no OAuth2GrantType implementation with same ID or shortcut like other grants' and does not identify which shortcut collided. The same race exists in getShortcutByGrantType (lazy refresh path), which does grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) and grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut) without any uniqueness check on the shortcut. If a misbehaving third-party provider returns a shortcut that collides with an existing one, this will silently corrupt the cached mapping at runtime.

findings.title: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is only set on the refresh path, not consistently on all token-issuance paths
findings.body: The grant-type attribute is set in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process, and (for refresh) TokenManager.validateToken. Any future caller of TokenManager.createClientAccessToken / initToken that does not first call one of these will silently fall back to the 'na' (unknown) shortcut in the encoded JTI. Constants.GRANT_TYPE is documented as the canonical key, but the responsibility for populating it is spread across many call sites with no guard. This should either be enforced inside createClientAccessToken/initToken (refuse to issue without a known grant type) or documented; otherwise the encoding will appear to work yet the encoded grant type will be 'na' for missed paths.

findings.title: getTokenContextFromTokenId will NPE on null input and does not validate token id length when no colon
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId(encodedTokenId) calls encodedTokenId.indexOf(':') without a null check. If it is called with a null token id (e.g. a token whose jti claim ended up null/unset, which is possible when no raw id was supplied), it will throw NullPointerException instead of returning the UNKNOWN context. Also, the decoder accepts 'no colon' strings of any length (including empty string) and treats the whole input as the raw id, which means a malformed token id that contains a colon later in the string (rather than as separator) could be parsed incorrectly because indexOf only finds the first ':'.

findings.title: OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType is captured at construction time but setFormParams can replace the params later
findings.body: The new grantType field is initialized once in the constructor from formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE), but the class still exposes setFormParams(...) which replaces the entire formParams map without updating grantType. Any flow that calls setFormParams after construction (the existence of that setter suggests it happens) will leave grantType pointing at the original form value, while getFormParams() returns the new one. The downstream constant Constants.GRANT_TYPE will then be the stale value, and the encoded JTI will carry the wrong grant shortcut.
